summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (labeled Book 10, part 35) in which Chloe and Arthur discuss a bookseller's secret: books should be placed everywhere people go, not confined to bookshops. Arthur explains his approach of having local kids curate anthologies from The Story So Far to match books to readers. Chloe gives Arthur a handmade birthday gift, a book wrapped in old backpack nylon and denim, and the scene shifts to a surreal ending involving The Story So Far and Great Expectations.
one_line: A fiction excerpt where Arthur explains his bookseller's secret of placing books everywhere, while Chloe gives him a handmade birthday book.
key_facts: Arthur says the secret of his bookshop was that it was not a bookshop, since bookshops were practically the only place to get a book at the time.
Newsagents might carry a few titles, but they were the same titles all around the country.
Arthur says the approach was about connecting kids with their local neighborhoods and the tastes there.
Arthur says kids were had curate their own anthologies of the best, most suitable material from The Story So Far.
Arthur summarizes his method as: the right book for the right person in the right place.
Arthur says you have to give people a religious experience before you can lure them into coming to church regularly.
Chloe says Arthur thinks reading is a religion.
Marcel asks whether reading is obsolete, and Arthur prepares to argue.
Chloe gives Arthur a carefully wrapped birthday package and says, 'Happy birthday, you old sod.'
The gift's cover is made from nylon from an old, old backpack and worn denim, with an embroidered title on the spine.
Chloe introduces Marcel to Arthur, and they shake hands.
Arthur moves on a carapace exoskeleton and is described as moving as spryly as a jaguar.
The excerpt ends with a character remarking 'Better than Great Expectations again' while digging through costumes on racks.
